Mayavi.note: Elder son of Mayasura. He came to the gates of Kishkindha at night to call Vali out over a woman and then ran, into a cave in the hills; Vali went in after him and told Sugriva to hold the mouth. After a year, with blood coming out and no voice, Sugriva took it for his brother's and rolled a rock across the entrance and went home to be crowned. Vali came out. Everything after it in Kishkindha — Sugriva driven off, Ruma taken, Rama's arrow from behind a tree — comes out of that cave. Rama 4.9

DundubhiAsura.name: Dundubhi
DundubhiAsura.note: Son of Mayasura, an asura in the shape of a buffalo, who went to the ocean and to the Himalaya looking for someone strong enough to fight and was sent on by both to Vali. Vali killed him and threw the carcass a yojana, and drops of the blood fell on Matanga's hermitage; the curse the sage laid for it — that Vali would die if he set foot on Rishyamuka — is the one patch of ground in the world where Sugriva was safe, and so the ground Rama finds him on. Rama 4.11

Devayani.note: First wife of Yayati; daughter of Shukracharya, preceptor of the asuras. Mother of Yadu and Turvasu. Loved Kacha, sent by the devas to learn Shukracharya's death-reviving mantra, and cursed his knowledge useless to him when he refused to marry a guru's daughter; pulled from a dry well by Yayati after Sharmishtha, her own attendant since a childhood quarrel, pushed her in; married Yayati on her father's insistence, on condition Sharmishtha never share his bed — a condition Yayati broke in secret, which is what drew Shukracharya's curse of old age down on him.

Sharmishtha.note: Second wife of Yayati; daughter of the asura king Vrishaparva. Mother of Druhyu, Anu and Puru. Made Devayani's handmaiden after pushing her into a well in a childhood quarrel over a garment; asked for Devayani as her own attendant instead as a face-saving condition of her father's surrender; secretly became Yayati's lover and bore him three sons under Devayani's own roof, discovery of which brought Shukracharya's curse down on the king.

people.Sunanda: Wife of Pratipa; a princess of Shibi and mother of Devapi, Bahlika and Shantanu.

Ganga.name: Ganga Devi
Ganga.note: The devi of the sacred river; Shantanu's first wife and mother of Bhishma, whom she bore as the last of the eight Vasus made mortal. Drowned her first seven infant sons at birth to return the cursed Vasus to heaven at once, and left Shantanu, as she had warned she would, the moment he broke his vow of never questioning her and asked why she drowned the eighth — sparing Bhishma, and raising him herself before returning him to his father.

Parashara.note: A great sage; father of Vyasa by Satyavati before her marriage to Shantanu.

people.Parishrami: A maidservant of the Kuru queens; mother of Vidura through Vyasa's niyoga.
people.Sughada: A vaishya attendant of the Kuru household; mother of Yuyutsu by Dhritarashtra.
people.Bhanumati: Wife of Duryodhana; a princess of Kalinga.
people.Hidimba: A rakshasi of the forest who loved Bhima during the Pandavas' exile; mother of Ghatotkacha.
people.Maurvi: Wife of Ghatotkacha; mother of Barbarika.
people.Rohini: Senior wife of Vasudeva; mother of Balarama and Subhadra.

Satyabhama.note: Daughter of Satrajit; the fiery queen who rode into battle beside Krishna against the demon Narakasura.

people.Jambavati: Daughter of the bear-king Jambavan; won when Krishna wrestled Jambavan for the Syamantaka gem. Mother of Samba.
people.Kalindi: The river Yamuna personified; she wed Krishna after long penance on its banks.
people.Mitravinda: An Avanti princess and Krishna's cousin, whom he carried off from her svayamvara.
people.Nagnajiti: Princess of Kosala (also called Satya), won by Krishna when he subdued her father's seven fierce bulls.
people.Bhadra: A Kekaya princess and Krishna's cousin, given to him by her brothers.
people.Lakshmana: A princess of Madra, won by Krishna at her svayamvara.
people.Usha: Daughter of the asura Banasura; she wed Aniruddha.
people.Revati: Daughter of King Raivata; born in an earlier age, she was shrunk to human height to become Balarama's wife.
people.Devika: A princess of the Shibi people; wife of Yudhishthira.
people.Vijaya: A princess won by Sahadeva at her svayamvara; his wife.

Shukracharya.note: Son of Bhrigu; guru and reviver of the asuras, keeper of the sanjivani mantra that raises the dead, which Kacha won from him at his own daughter Devayani's insistence. Warned Bali not to grant Vamana's request and was ignored; cursed Devayani's husband Yayati with old age for breaking his word to her over Sharmishtha.

Vishvamitra.note: A king who won brahmarshi-hood by fierce penance; father of Shakuntala by the apsara Menaka. By name — born Kaushika, a kshatriya king who warred with Vasishtha over the wish-cow Nandini and lost, then renounced his throne for penance to become a brahmin's equal; sent Menaka to break that penance, and lost decades of it to her before renewing his resolve; created a rival heaven for Trishanku when the devas refused him; adopted Shunahshepha as Devarata over his own sons' protest; and served finally as Rama's own guru and escort to Mithila, generations after his quarrels with Vasishtha.

Jambavan.note: The immortal bear-king of the Ramayan age; Krishna wrestled him for the Syamantaka gem and won his daughter Jambavati.

Raivata.note: King Raivata (Kakudmi), who took his daughter Revati to Brahma's realm and returned an age later to a world grown small.

Dantavakra.note: King of Karusha, son of Shrutadeva; a rebirth of the same doorkeeper of Vishnu as Shishupala, and like him slain by Krishna.

Shuka.note: Son of Vyasa, born radiant and already renounced; the sage who first recited the Bhagavata.

Tara.note: Wife of Brihaspati, guru of the devas; Chandra bore her away, and of that union was born Budha, sparking the war of the devas and asuras.

RohiniNakshatra.name: Rohini
RohiniNakshatra.note: Favourite among Chandra's twenty-seven wives, the nakshatras, daughters of Daksha.

people.Sudakshina: Queen of Dilipa, princess of the Magadha line; mother of Raghu.
people.Indumati: Princess who chose Aja at her svayamvara; queen of Aja and mother of Dasharatha.
people.Kausalya: Chief queen of Dasharatha and mother of Rama; a princess of Dakshina Kosala.
people.Sumitra: Third queen of Dasharatha; mother of the twins Lakshmana and Shatrughna.
people.Sunayana: Queen of Janaka; foster-mother of Sita and mother of Urmila.
people.Mandodari: Daughter of Mayasura; the wise and virtuous chief queen of Ravana and mother of Indrajit.
people.Vajrajwala: Wife of Kumbhakarna; a granddaughter of the demon Virochana.

Rishyasringa.note: A sage raised without knowledge of women; his coming ended a drought, and his fire-rite gave Dasharatha his four sons. Husband of Shanta.

SulochanaR.name: Sulochana
SulochanaR.note: Wife of Indrajit (Meghanada), daughter of the naga king Shesha; on his death she followed him onto the pyre.

Sarama.note: Rakshasi wife of Vibhishana; she comforted Sita in captivity.

Lopamudra.note: Princess fashioned for the sage Agastya; his learned wife and a hymn-seer in her own right.

Narmada.note: Sister of the Nagas, given to Purukutsa by her serpent brothers at Vasuki's bidding, and the river of that name. SB 9.7.2

Gopali.note: The apsara who took the form of a cowherd woman and bore Gargya his son. Called Rambha in some recensions. HV 58

Adrika.note: An apsara cursed into a fish in the Yamuna. She swallowed the seed of Uparichara Vasu and bore twins: the boy who founded the Matsya kingdom, and the girl Satyavati, who was raised by fishermen. MBh 1.57

Makari.note: The makara of the ocean who swallowed a drop of Hanuman's sweat as he cooled himself after burning Lanka, and conceived Makardhwaja by it. The Indian retellings leave her unnamed and call her only the makara, so she carries the creature's name here; the Thai Ramakien names her Suvannamaccha and makes her a mermaid, and Ravana's daughter. Krittivasi Ramayana; Ramakien

Dyumatsena.note: Blind king of Shalva, deposed and exiled to the forest; father of Satyavan. Regained both his sight and his throne the moment his son was restored to life, on Yama's earlier boon to Savitri. MBh 3.277-283.

JaratkaruSage.name: Jaratkaru
JaratkaruSage.note: Ascetic sage; refused to marry until his ancestors, seen hanging over a pit by a fraying rope of grass, told him only a son could save them, and that the son must share his own name. Vasuki gave him his sister, also named Jaratkaru, on that condition alone. Left her, as he had warned he would at the first word he took as disrespect, once Astika was conceived. MBh 1.13-16.

KrishashvaRishi.name: Krishashva
KrishashvaRishi.note: A husband of two of Daksha's daughters, Archis and Dhishana, by whom he fathered the comet Dhumaketu and four more sons. Not Krishashva the Ikshvaku king who came before Senajit, already in this tree several eras later -- the archive's own namesake table already lists them as distinct men. SB 6.6.2, 20

Vibhandaka.note: Son of Kashyap. The apsara Urvashi passed while he was at his austerities and his seed fell in the water; a doe drank it and bore him Rishyasringa, who came out with a horn on his head. He raised the boy in the deep forest without letting him see a woman, a village or a road, and was away for fuel when the courtesans of Anga came for him. Rama 1.9-10

Shalva.note: King of Saubha, the flying city. Amba had chosen him before Bhishma carried her and her sisters off from the svayamvara at Kashi; when Bhishma learned it and sent her back, Shalva would not take a woman another man had already won in the hall, and it is that second refusal, not the first, that leaves her with nowhere to go and turns her into the vow that becomes Shikhandi. Long after, to avenge Shishupala, he besieged Dvaraka in Saubha itself and Krishna brought the city down and killed him. MBh 5.170-175; SB 10.76-77

Sanda.note: Son of Shukracharya. He and his brother Marka kept the palace school in Hiranyakashipu's house and were set to teach Prahlada politics and the three worldly ends. The boy would not stop saying the name of the enemy, so they beat it out of him, coaxed it out of him, and finally handed him back to his father as unteachable — having in the meantime lost the whole class to him. SB 7.5

Marka.note: Son of Shukracharya, brother of Sanda and of Devayani; with his brother, tutor to Prahlada in Hiranyakashipu's court. SB 7.5

Yajnavalkya.note: The sage of Janaka's court and of the white Yajurveda, which he got direct from the sun after giving back, in a quarrel, everything he had learned from his teacher Vaishampayana — who was his uncle. At Janaka's sacrifice a thousand cows with gold on their horns stood in the yard for whoever was the best of the brahmins there, and he simply told his pupil to drive them home, and then answered everything the hall could put to him. Brihadaranyaka 3, 4.5; Shatapatha Brahmana 14

Maitreyi.note: The wife of Yajnavalkya who, when he was leaving for the forest and dividing his property between his two wives, asked whether all the wealth in the world would make her deathless — was told it would not, that it only makes a comfortable life — and said then what would she do with something that did not make her immortal, and asked for what he knew instead. What he tells her, that a husband is not dear for the husband's sake but for the sake of the self, is the passage the Upanishad is usually opened at. Brihadaranyaka 2.4, 4.5

Katyayani.note: The second wife of Yajnavalkya, who took the household half when he left. The Brihadaranyaka says of her only that her understanding was a woman's understanding of a woman's things, and does not say it unkindly; the two wives are set beside each other and not ranked. Brihadaranyaka 2.4.1, 4.5.1

Gargi.name: Gargi Vachaknavi
Gargi.note: Of the Garga line; the one questioner in Janaka's hall allowed to ask twice. She asked what water is woven on, and on what that, and kept climbing, world upon world, until Yajnavalkya told her not to ask past the imperishable or her head would fall off — and she stopped, turned to the hall and told them that none of them was going to beat this man, and sat down. Then she got up and asked again anyway. Brihadaranyaka 3.6, 3.8

Galava.note: Vishvamitra's pupil, who would not go without paying a teacher's fee and would not stop asking what it should be, until Vishvamitra said, to be rid of him: eight hundred horses white as moonlight with one black ear. There are only six hundred such horses in the world. Yayati, asked for them and having none, gave him his daughter Madhavi instead, and Galava lent her to three kings in turn, two hundred horses for one son each, and gave Vishvamitra the six hundred horses and Madhavi herself for the remaining two hundred. She had a boon that made her a virgin again after each birth, which is what made her lendable, and at the end of it she was offered a svayamvara and chose the forest. MBh 5.104-121

Mandavya.note: The sage the king's men impaled on a stake, having found thieves' goods left at his hermitage and no answer from a man under a vow of silence. He lived on the stake, and they could not get him off it, and they cut it short and left it in him — Ani-Mandavya, Mandavya of the spike. He went to Dharma and asked what he had done to earn it; told that as a small boy he had pushed reeds through insects, he said that a child does not know and that no scripture puts a boy's game against a life on a stake, and cursed Dharma to be born a man, and of a shudra woman. That birth is Vidura. MBh 1.101

Valmiki.note: The first poet. The Ramayan calls him Pracetasa, son of Pracetas — a name of Varuna — and that is the only parentage the poem itself gives him; the later story of Ratnakara the highwayman, sat down to repeat a name he could not say until it came out backwards and became his own, is the Skanda Purana's. He is in his own poem: he takes Sita in when Rama puts her away, raises Lava and Kusha in the hermitage, teaches them the poem about their father, and sends them to sing it in his court to his face. No wife and no child of his own are named anywhere, so he stands here alone, which is what the texts say of him. Rama 1.2, 7.93-96; Skanda Purana

unions.note: Rama 1.9-10. The mother is the doe, and gets no record.
